text: Early stopping in training stops when validation performance stops improving, preventing the model from learning noise. This is commonly used in neural networks with many epochs.
Data augmentation artificially increases the training set by applying transformations, reducing overfitting in vision tasks. For images, rotations, flipping, and color shifts create variability.

Optimization in machine learning involves finding model parameters that minimize a loss function. Gradient descent iteratively updates parameters in the direction of negative gradient, with learning rate determining step size.

Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) uses a random subset (mini-batch) to estimate gradient, reducing computation and adding noise that can help escape local minima. It is widely used for large datasets.
Momentum accelerates convergence by accumulating past gradients, smoothing updates. This helps navigate ravines and reduces oscillations. Nesterov accelerated gradient looks ahead.
Adaptive learning rate methods like AdaGrad, RMSProp, and Adam adjust learning rates per parameter. Adam combines momentum and RMSProp, often performing well in practice with less tuning.
The loss landscape can have many local minima and saddle points. Optimization algorithms are designed to escape saddle points where gradient is zero but not minimum. Stochasticity helps.

Embeddings are dense vector representations of discrete items (words, users, products) in a continuous space, where similarity reflects semantic or functional relationships. They are learned from data.
Word2vec trains embeddings by predicting context words (skip-gram) or predicting target from context (CBOW). The embeddings capture analogies: king - man + woman is approximately queen.
GloVe (Global Vectors) uses matrix factorization of co-occurrence statistics to produce embeddings, balancing global corpus statistics with local context.
Embeddings are crucial for transfer learning in NLP, where pretrained embeddings like BERT or ELMo provide contextual representations. They can be fine-tuned for specific tasks.
In recommendation systems, user and item embeddings are learned to capture preferences, using matrix factorization or collaborative filtering. Dot product predicts preference.

Transformers are a neural network architecture based on self-attention mechanisms, enabling parallel processing of sequences. They have become the dominant architecture in NLP and are expanding to vision.

Self-attention computes weighted sums of values based on similarity between queries and keys. This allows the model to focus on relevant parts of the input, capturing long-range dependencies without recurrence.

Multi-head attention runs several attention heads in parallel, each projecting to different subspaces, allowing the model to attend to different aspects. The outputs are concatenated and linearly transformed.
Positional encoding is added to input embeddings because transformers have no inherent sense of order. Sinusoidal encodings or learned embeddings provide position information.
The transformer encoder consists of multiple layers, each with multi-head attention and feed-forward networks, with residual connections and layer normalization. BERT is an encoder-only model.

Training is the process of updating model parameters using a dataset and an optimization algorithm, requiring forward and backward passes. Inference is using the trained model to make predictions on new data.

During training, gradients are computed and parameters adjusted; this is computationally expensive and needs large memory. Inference only requires a forward pass, which is faster and can be optimized.
Batch normalization and dropout behave differently in training and inference: during training they use batch statistics and dropout, while during inference they use fixed statistics and no dropout.
The goal of training is to minimize loss on training data and generalize; inference focuses on speed and accuracy. Trade-offs may involve model quantization or pruning to accelerate inference.
Training typically requires labeled data, while inference can handle unlabeled inputs. The quality of inference depends on how well the model generalizes.

Hypothesis testing compares observations with random variation expected under a null hypothesis. A p-value is not the probability that the null hypothesis is true. Statistical significance does not imply a large practical effect.

Probability represents uncertainty with values between zero and one. Mutual exclusivity and independence describe different relationships and should not be confused. Conditional probability updates a judgment when new information becomes available.
Bayes' theorem combines prior beliefs with new evidence. Likelihood describes how plausible the observed data are under a particular hypothesis.
